properties.description:
SVRTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
East Central Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 330 PM MST.

* At 256 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 10 miles southwest
of Portal, moving east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damage to vehicles is expected.

* Locations impacted include...
Portal, Paradise and Rucker Canyon.

This includes Route 80 between mile markers 409 and 415.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing large hail.

properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Tuesday, for the Mon
Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 19 at 12:05PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong storm system is expected to move into the northern half of
the Alaska Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast tonight and
continue through Tuesday. Beginning tonight for Haines, Skagway, and
the two highways, periods of moderate to heavy rain will move over
the area. Total rain accumulation are expected to be between 1.5-3.5
inches, with the heaviest rain late Tuesday morning into Tuesday
afternoon. While substantial areal flooding is not expected at this
time, isolated instances of minor ponding of water in low lying
areas are possible. Furthermore, wet snow is possibly on the
Klondike Highway near White Pass up to 3 inches through tonight,
though warm surface temperatures may hinder these snow totals.

surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
